_comment: Model catalog for ./run.sh. Edit this file to add models; run.sh reads it with jq and
never needs changing. `./run.sh --help` prints the alias list straight from here.
Every key under `defaults` is applied to every model unless the model overrides it.
`continuous_batching` must stay true: cli.py:252 leaves scheduler_config = None without
it, so max_num_seqs / cache_memory_mb / every kv_cache_* key is parsed and discarded.
There is deliberately no `downloaded` flag — run.sh probes the cache at runtime so this
file cannot go stale.
Used by `--multi`, by the auto-merge path when a port is already busy, and by
bare `./run.sh <name>` (elastic single-model serve, capped to one resident model —
see max_resident_models below). Every catalog alias is ALWAYS registered on the
port, not just the ones named on the command line — any of them can load lazily
on request (downloading first if needed), which is what makes /v1/models list the
whole catalog and what lets a client ask for anything without a restart.
memory_budget_gb is what makes 'load both, or evict one' a runtime decision:
models load lazily and are evicted per contention_policy when the budget is tight.
Left unset (as here), run.sh derives it at launch time from THIS machine's actual
RAM (RUN_SH_RAM_BUDGET_FRACTION, default 0.75x hw.memsize) instead of a number that
would silently over- or under-commit on a different Mac — set it explicitly here to
pin a fixed value again. Either way `--multi` with no names on the command line also
trims default_multi (below) to whatever combination of it fits that budget, by each
model's size_gb, warning about anything it had to drop.
max_resident_models is a second, count-based cap alongside the byte budget — set
to 1 to force exactly one resident model regardless of how much budget is left
(that's what bare `./run.sh <name>` uses); leave null/omitted for `--multi` so it
stays purely budget-gated as before. Eviction picks the lowest-`priority` resident
model first (models.json per-entry `priority`, default 0 via `defaults`), idle time
only breaks ties within the same priority.
reasoning_parser/tool_call_parser are PROCESS-GLOBAL — RegisteredModel
(model_registry.py:145) has no per-model parser fields — so every model merged onto
one port shares these. run.sh warns when a merged model wanted different ones.
default_multi is what `./run.sh --multi` (no names given) falls back to — every
alias a local client (e.g. Prism, config at ~/.config/prism/llm.env) actually
requests. It no longer drives the bare-invocation default (that's elastic single,
one resident model at a time, on `default: true` below) — two models concurrently
resident measurably capped GPU utilization, so bare `./run.sh` went back to one.
